Regional priority programs and projects
Endorsement, or recommendations
Reconfirm ongoing programs and projects. Encode new or updated ones: cost per year, physical and financial progress
Head of agency endorses the submission (example window: 8 November to 6 December 2024)
Only submissions marked "as endorsed" are processed
Check each entry against the PIP criteria and the scope of the TRIP
ICC REVIEW applies to projects of PHP 5 billion or more funded by the national budget, to PPP projects, and to every project funded by a foreign loan
Project proposal with feasibility study and financing plan
Technical, economic and financial appraisal
Recommendation
Approval or confirmation

Tier 2 proposals in OSBPS (a different system from PIPOL)
After the budget is known, update yearly costs to match the GAA and the National Expenditure Program

GAP REPORTED BY THE PFM REFORMS ROADMAP AND ITS ACTION PLAN: PIPOL and OSBPS are separate systems, and no standard project identifier connects an entry with a line of the budget proposal. A working group of DEPDev and DBM was created to link them. An integrated planning and budgeting tool is planned.

03a.title: 03a  Budget preparation: from the fiscal program to the President's budget (example: FY 2027 budget, prepared in 2026)

items.text: Fiscal program: revenue, spending ceiling, deficit, borrowing
Budget Call (National Budget Memorandum No. 156): policy, budget levels, forms, calendar. Budget Forum 28-29 January 2026
Forward Estimates for FY 2027-2029, formulated by DBM with the agency (basis of Tier 1)
Internal call for proposals
Regional proposals for priority programs and projects
Inputs and recommendations (BP Form C). DEPDev regional offices send consolidated RDC resolutions to DBM
Consultation on proposed programs
Inputs (reported in BP Form D)
TIER 1: cost of ongoing programs and commitments at the same scope and quality (BP Forms 201-A to 201-D, 204, 205, 100 series, A and B). Submission period 6 March to 28 April 2026
TIER 2: new or expanded programs and projects (BP Form 202, and 203 for foreign-assisted projects), implementation-ready and endorsed
Two printed copies. The electronic copy prevails
Encoded proposals
Technical budget hearings: the agency justifies its proposal
Evaluation and executive review. Tier 2 proposals compete for the fiscal space (spending program minus total Tier 1)
Proposed budget levels
Recommended budget
Approval by the President and the Cabinet
Prepare the budget documents: National Expenditure Program (NEP), Budget of Expenditures and Sources of Financing (BESF), President's Budget Message, staffing summary
Submit the budget within 30 days from the opening of the regular session (for FY 2027: by 26 August 2026. Press reports: submitted on 11 August 2026)
LIMIT SET BY THE CONSTITUTION: Congress may not increase the appropriations recommended by the President for the operation of the government as specified in the budget.

items.text: President's budget: NEP, BESF, Budget Message, within 30 days from the opening of the regular session
The NEP is filed as the General Appropriations Bill (GAB) and referred to the committee
Briefing on the economy and the fiscal program
Hearings, agency by agency: plans, past performance
Answers and documents

Answers and documents

Plenary debates and amendments. Approval on second and third reading
GAB as approved by the House

Plenary debates and amendments. Approval on second and third reading
LIMITS ON CONGRESS: it may not increase the appropriations recommended by the President. Every provision must relate to a specific appropriation in the bill (no rider).
House conferees and House version
Senate conferees and Senate version
Reconcile the two versions
Conference report
Conference report
Both chambers ratify. The enrolled bill goes to the President
Review. May veto particular items. The items not vetoed become law
Signed General Appropriations Act (GAA)
Override by two thirds of each chamber

IF NO GAA IS PASSED BY THE END OF THE FISCAL YEAR: the GAA of the previous year is deemed re-enacted and stays in force until the new bill is passed. Example: the FY 2025 GAA was re-enacted from 1 to 4 January 2026. The FY 2026 GAA (Republic Act No. 12314) took effect on 5 January 2026.

Release guidelines for the year (National Budget Circular)
Budget execution documents: BED 1 Financial Plan, BED 2 Physical Plan, BED 3 Monthly Disbursement Program
Documents for evaluation

Approval

AUTHORITY TO PAY = CASH AUTHORITY
Cash position of the national government

Advice of NCA Issued
Agency downloads the advice
Request for additional NCA
Additional NCA

06b.title: 06b  Competitive bidding under the New Government Procurement Act (RA 12009): who does what, with the time limits

participants.BAC: Bids and Awards Committee (BAC) with Secretariat and working group

items.text: Purchase request, specifications, bidding documents for an item in the Annual Procurement Plan
Are appropriations available for this procurement?
Confirmation: the item is in the budget law, or in the proposed budget for early procurement
Pre-procurement conference: the procurement follows the plan, appropriations are available, the award criterion is chosen
Post the invitation to bid and the bidding documents, with the budget for the contract and the source of funding. Also on the website of the entity, and 7 days at its premises
Notice visible to registered suppliers
Pre-bid conference, at least 12 days before the deadline for bids (required from a budget of PHP 3 million)
Bids in two sealed envelopes: technical (with eligibility documents and bid security) and financial. Deadline: at most 45 days (goods), 50 or 65 (works), 75 (consulting) after posting
Invitation to observe each stage: at least two observers, in addition to the representative of COA
Opening of bids immediately after the deadline. Each envelope passes or fails. A bid above the approved budget for the contract is rejected
Bid evaluation: 7 days for the lowest calculated bid, 14 days when quality is rated with price, 21 days for consulting. Rank by the award criterion

branches.label: Until one bidder passes, starting from the first in rank

items.text: Post-qualification within 12 days: verify the legal, technical and financial documents, with the latest tax returns
Recommendation of award, with the document that authorizes the entity to incur the obligation
Approval within 10 days, then the notice of award immediately
Award published
Performance security, before signing: 5 percent (goods, consulting) or 10 percent (works) of the contract price, 30 percent as a surety bond
Contract signed within 10 days from receipt of the notice of award
Notice to proceed within 3 days from approval of the contract
Observation report (also to PhilGEPS, and copies to the GPPB and the Ombudsman)
Observation report

TOTAL TIME: from the opening of bids to the award, not more than 60 days. The period does not run while an early procurement waits for the budget law. FOUR AWARD CRITERIA: lowest calculated responsive bid (goods, works), most economically advantageous responsive bid (quality and price), most advantageous responsive bid (highest quality), highest rated responsive bid (consulting services). All days are calendar days.

EARLY PROCUREMENT: all steps up to the recommendation may be done before the budget law, once the proposed budget is submitted. No award until the funding is approved and in effect and the final procurement plan is approved.
Request for reconsideration within 3 days. The BAC decides within 7 days
Protest within 7 days, filed electronically, with a fee that is not returned. Decision within 7 days. It is final for smaller contracts. For the others: review by the Regional Trial Court

07a.title: 07a  From obligation to payment: who certifies what, and which record each step writes (goods bought by a national agency, paid by payment order)

participants.HEAD: Head of agency or authorized official

items.text: COMMIT. The supplier is chosen (chapter 06). The agency records the obligation and certifies that funds are available.
Obligation Request and Status (ORS) with the contract or purchase order. Box A: charges are necessary, lawful and under my direct supervision, and the supporting documents are valid, proper and legal
Check the allotment in the registry. Assign the ORS number. Enter the obligation in the registry. Box B: allotment available and obligated. No journal entry
Purchase order or contract with the certificate of the chief accountant: "Funds Available", and the number, date and amount of the ORS
Signed purchase order or contract
VERIFY. The amount becomes a payable only after delivery and acceptance.
Delivery, with delivery receipt and invoice

Inspection and acceptance report with the numbers of the purchase order and of the invoice. Inspection officer: inspected, verified and found in order as to quantity and specifications. Property custodian: accepted, complete or partial
Copy of the acceptance report, with the purchase order and the delivery receipt
Journal entry voucher (JEV): debit the asset or expense, credit Accounts Payable. The budget unit enters the payable in part C of the ORS
APPROVE THE CLAIM. One disbursement voucher (DV) in four copies.
DV with the original acceptance report, delivery receipt, purchase order and a copy of the ORS. Box A: expenses necessary, lawful and incurred under my direct supervision
Check the documents against a list. Assign the DV number. Look into the index of payments: was this claim paid before? Compare the DV with the ORS. Box B: the accounting entry

Head of accounting looks into the registry of the NCA. If the balance is enough: enter the amount as used, and sign Box C: cash available, supporting documents complete, amount claimed proper. If not: keep the DV until cash is available
DV for approval
Box D: approved for payment
PAY. The payment order is the LDDAP-ADA: a list of payees with bank account, ORS number, gross amount, tax and net amount, and an advice to the bank.
LDDAP-ADA in five copies for the approved DVs. The chief accountant signs "Certified Correct"
Signs "Approved"
Enter it in the record of checks and payment orders, with the new balance of the NCA. The cashier signs the advice to debit the account
LDDAP-ADA for the second signature
Countersigns the advice to debit the account
Stamp "PAID" on the payment order, the DVs and the documents. Prepare the summary list (SLIIE) in four copies. The cashier certifies it, the head of agency approves it
Summary list and LDDAP-ADA (paper copies, or through the electronic facility of the bank)
Check the payment order and the NCA balance. Debit the MDS sub-account of the agency
Credit the account of the payee with the net amount, not earlier than 24 hours and not later than 48 hours after receipt
One copy of the summary list and of the LDDAP-ADA on the same day
Replenishment from the Treasury Single Account
Validated copy of the LDDAP-ADA. Items that could not be credited are marked as not paid
Official receipt, or other evidence that the payment was received
Daily report of payment orders issued (RADAI) in four copies, with the DVs and the validated LDDAP-ADA
JEV for the payment: debit Accounts Payable, credit Cash-MDS, Regular and Due to BIR. Enter it in the journal of payment orders
One copy of the RADAI. The budget unit enters the payment in part C of the ORS and the disbursement in the registry
Tax withheld: returns filed in the electronic system of BIR, paid by Tax Remittance Advice by the 10th day of the next month. No cash moves
AFTER PAYMENT
First copy of the RADAI and of the JEV, with the original DV, its documents and the validated LDDAP-ADA
Audit observations, or notices of suspension or disallowance (chapter 09)

IN AGENCIES THAT USE BTMS: obligation request, purchase order, goods received note, voucher and journal entry are records in one system. The system refuses an obligation above the allotment and a payment above the cash allocation, and it creates the journal entry from the voucher.

07d.title: 07d  Payment and settlement: how money moves from the Treasury Single Account to the payee (Modified Disbursement System)

items.text: NCA: limit for the MDS sub-account of the agency
Books: debit Cash-MDS, Regular, credit Subsidy from National Government. Registry of the NCA. No official receipt is issued for an NCA
Payment order (LDDAP-ADA) in three copies and summary list (SLIIE) in two, on paper or through the electronic facility of the bank
Books, on the day of the daily report: credit Cash-MDS, Regular
Check the payment order and the NCA balance. Debit the MDS sub-account (the NCA balance decreases)

branches.label: Payee has an account in the same bank

items.text: Direct credit, not earlier than 24 hours and not later than 48 hours after receipt

branches.label: Payee has an account in another bank

items.text: Bank transfer. The payee bears the bank charge
One copy of the summary list and of the payment order on the same day: notice of the amount to be replenished
Instruction to replenish the servicing bank
Debit the Treasury account, credit the account of the bank at BSP
Books of the Treasury: debit Subsidy to NGAs, credit Cash in Bank
Validated copy of the payment order. Items that could not be credited are marked
For an item not credited: journal entry to cancel it, and a new payment order. Each month: reconcile the books with the bank statement of the sub-account

PAYMENT BY CHECK (exception): an MDS check is drawn on the account of the Treasurer of the Philippines. The agency sends the bank an Advice of Checks Issued and Cancelled at least daily, so that the payees can cash the checks. The bank treats a check as stale after six months.

END OF QUARTER: the unused balance of a regular NCA lapses. Books of the agency: debit Subsidy from National Government, credit Cash-MDS, Regular. IN AGENCIES THAT USE BTMS: payments are made by electronic transfer (PESONet, InstaPay) or check, and the system reconciles with electronic bank statements each day.

07i.title: 07i  A works contract with an advance, progress billings and retention money (example of the Manual)

participants.ENG: Project unit and engineer of the agency

items.text: BEFORE THE WORK
Performance security before the contract is signed. In the example: cash of 75,000. Books: Guaranty/Security Deposits Payable 75,000
Obligation for the whole contract price: 800,000 in the registry. No journal entry
Written request for an advance, with a letter of credit, a bank guarantee or a surety bond
Advance of 15 percent: 120,000. Books: debit Advances to Contractors 120,000, credit Cash-MDS, Regular 120,000
FIRST PROGRESS BILLING: 50 percent of the work
Statement of work accomplished: 400,000
The engineer checks the statement and certifies the amount to be paid
Books: debit Construction in Progress 400,000. Credit Advances to Contractors 60,000 (half of the advance is recovered) and Accounts Payable 340,000
Payment of 282,200. Books: debit Accounts Payable 340,000. Credit Cash-MDS, Regular 282,200, Guaranty/Security Deposits Payable 34,000 (retention), Due to BIR 23,800 (tax withheld)
FINAL BILLING: the other 50 percent, completed late
Statement of work accomplished: 400,000. Certificate of completion
Books: debit Construction in Progress 400,000. Credit Advances to Contractors 60,000 and Accounts Payable 340,000
Damages for the delay: 8,000, collected in cash. Books: Miscellaneous Income 8,000
Payment of 282,200. Retention 34,000. Tax withheld 23,800
Turn-over of the building. Books: debit Buildings 800,000, credit Construction in Progress 800,000
AFTER FINAL ACCEPTANCE
Release of the retention money: 68,000. Books: debit Guaranty/Security Deposits Payable 68,000, credit Cash-MDS, Regular 68,000
Return of the performance security: 75,000

Appeal

Action plan on the recommendations
COA annual report on the financial condition and operation of the government, by 30 September

participants.BO: BIR office that processes the claim

items.text: CLAIM
Claim for refund with documents. Kinds: input VAT on zero-rated sales, tax collected by error, excess creditable withholding tax, conversion of a tax credit certificate into cash
Verify the claim within the time limit (180 days for regular claims, 90 days for VAT claims)
Recommendation

PAYMENT FROM THE AMOUNT "TAX REFUND" IN THE BIR BUDGET

Same fiscal program, with the financing program

Project proposal for ICC review
ICC recommendation, ED Council approval

Forward Obligational Authority (project loan)

Attested appointment

Annual investment program from the approved local development plan
Income estimate and recommended spending ceiling by sector, based on the approved local plans
Budget call with the ceilings
Statements of income and expenditures
Budget proposals, on or before 15 July
Review and budget hearings
Executive budget, not later than 16 October
AUTHORIZATION
Enact the appropriation ordinance on or before the end of the current fiscal year, within the legal limits (see 14b)
Ordinance for approval

branches.label: No ordinance at the start of the fiscal year

items.text: Stay in session, with no other business. After 90 days the ordinance of the previous year is deemed reenacted, only for salaries, statutory and contractual obligations, and essential operating expenses
REVIEW BY A HIGHER AUTHORITY

Copy of the ordinance. DBM reviews provinces, highly urbanized cities, independent component cities, and municipalities in Metro Manila. The provincial sanggunian reviews component cities and municipalities

Ordinance declared inoperative in whole or in part. The treasurer may not pay from those items

Release allotments. Collect local taxes and fees

Statement of receipts and expenditures to BLGF (eSRE), quarterly and annual. Accounts to COA
COA audit report

participants.SP: Sanggunian of the city or municipality

items.text: PREPARATION AND ENACTMENT
Estimate of income for the next year, and statements of income and expenditure, on or before 15 September

Prepare the budget with the treasurer. Mandatory items: 10 percent of the general fund for the youth council, at least 20 percent of the tax allotment for development, 5 percent of regular income for calamities. Personal services at most 55 percent of last year's income
Budget, on or before 16 October
Appropriation ordinance, by a majority of all members. The punong barangay votes only when the votes are equal and has no veto
REVIEW
Ordinance, within 10 days after enactment
Ordinance with findings
Review within 60 days: legal requirements and limits are met, appropriations do not exceed estimated income
The ordinance is deemed to be in full force

branches.label: Found inoperative, in whole or in part

items.text: Returned for adjustment. The treasurer may make no further payments from the inoperative part
EXECUTION AND ACCOUNTS
Custody of the funds. Collections and payments
Records of transactions. The accounts are kept in the offices of the barangay treasurer and of the city or municipal accountant
If no ordinance is enacted, the ordinance of the earlier year is deemed re-enacted, for salaries, obligations fixed by law or contract, and essential operating expenses only

FAR 1-C each quarter: obligations, disbursements, liquidations and balances of fund transfers
The auditor of the implementing body audits its payments. The auditor of the source agency audits the transfer

15f.title: 15f  Cash aid to persons: from the list of beneficiaries to the credit in each account

items.text: WHO HAS A RIGHT TO THE MONEY
Program law: who qualifies, conditions, kinds of grant. Budget law: the amount for the year
Select households with a standardized targeting system. Check the list again every three years
Amount of each grant, as fixed by the advisory council of the program and reviewed every six years
EACH PAYMENT PERIOD
Check that each household met the conditions (for example school attendance, health visits)
Payroll of beneficiaries for the period, certified and approved. Obligation recorded against the allotment
Cash authority (NCA) for the period (chapter 05)
Payment order with the list of accounts, within the cash authority
Grant credited to the account of the household, or paid out by a remittance institution
Report of amounts credited and of amounts not credited
RECORDS AND REVIEW
Accounting entries. Amounts not credited are returned or paid again
Yearly report on the program, before the President's budget message
Independent monitoring committee, and audit by COA
The books of the agency show one payment for many persons. The evidence that each person was paid is in the records of the bank.

16f.title: 16f  Public verification of DBM release documents with a blockchain record

items.text: Approved release document (SARO, or advice of NCA)
Record of the issued document
Store a fingerprint of the document (a hash) with date and document number. The record cannot be changed later
Document for download, with a QR code
Copy of the document (for example to a contractor or a bank)
Scan the QR code, or enter the document reference
Retrieve the record
Stored record
Result: the copy matches the issued document, or it does not
WHAT A MATCH PROVES: DBM issued this document with this content. WHAT IT DOES NOT PROVE: that the release was correct, that the agency obligated or paid the amount, or that anything was delivered.

RELATED BILL: the CADENA bill would require wider publication of budget data on a digital ledger. The Senate passed it in December 2025. In early October 2026 it was still pending in the House of Representatives.

RELATED ORDER: Executive Order No. 126 of 28 September 2026 makes the COMPASS portal the platform for budget disclosures. The order allows the portal to use distributed ledger technology such as a blockchain. It does not require it.
